subject: general
question: Which of the following soils has the highest water-retaining capacity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Black Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Black soil**, also known as Regur soil, has the highest water-retaining capacity due to its high clay content.
 
• It is predominantly found in the **Deccan Plateau regions** of India, including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• The soil is rich in nutrients like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, which further enhance its ability to retain moisture.
 
• Black soil is highly suitable for cultivating crops like **cotton, sugarcane, wheat, and pulses** due to its moisture-retaining ability.
 
• Its unique property of forming deep cracks during dry seasons helps in air circulation and improves soil fertility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water-retaining capacity:**

 
 
• This refers to the ability of soil to hold water and make it available for plant growth.
 
• Clayey soils, like black soil, have a higher water-retaining capacity compared to sandy soils.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil:**
 
 
• Found in areas with high iron oxide content, giving it a reddish appearance.
 
• It has low water-retaining capacity and is less fertile compared to black soil.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil:**
 
 
• Highly fertile and found in river basins, but its water-retaining capacity is moderate.
 
• Suitable for crops like rice, wheat, and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Desert Soil:**
 
 
• Found in arid regions like Rajasthan and Gujarat.
 
• It is sandy, has very low water-retaining capacity, and requires irrigation for cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Clay content importance:**
 
 
• Clay particles are small and have a high surface area, allowing them to retain moisture effectively.
 
• Soils with higher clay content are generally better at holding water and nutrients.
